messages:
elaine: Heads up — in the quant canary (raven-q8-v2) we're seeing structured output blows up when there's a long conversation prefix + kv-cache hit. A few examples where the model emits truncated JSON (missing trailing ] or a closing brace) causing parser failures.

elaine: repro snippet pasted from canary logs:

elaine: ```
Input prefix (user/system): ...  // long context trimmed
Model output (tokens): {
  "items": [
    {"id": "abc", "score": 0.92},
    {"id": "def", "score": 0.88}
  "meta": {"source": "kb"}
```
(ends abruptly)

elaine: This only shows up when kvcache prefix > ~1200 tokens and we use model-quantized decode profile with continuous batching. On unquantized it's fine. Thoughts?

matt: hmm, sounds like token-level truncation mid-JSON. Any chance the runtime is dropping partial token tails at batch boundaries? We toggled a change last week to speed up KV stitching.

elaine: yeah timeline matches. We rolled runtime patch: kvcache/fast-stitch v1.3. It drops last 2 tokens when it detects an incomplete token from peer shard. The idea was to avoid malformed byte sequences, but looks like it can break structured outputs.

priya: can we detect parse-failures and automatically retry with a small repair flow? e.g. if JSON.parse fails then call model with a tiny prompt: "You returned malformed JSON. Fix and return only valid JSON that matches schema X." with lower temperature. That usually heals minor truncations.

zach: yep that's the quick mitigation. Also consider a heuristic pre-check: if output ends with an open bracket/brace, append a short continuation probe like "\n}" or "\n]" and run parse again — but that's risky for arbitrary schemas.

matt: long-term we should avoid dropping tokens that matter for structured outputs. Options:
- revert the fast-stitch change and fix underlying byte handling
- make fast-stitch keep at least N UTF-8 codepoint boundaries and avoid chopping when prefix contains open JSON delimiters
- or at runtime set a flag to preserve the last 256 tokens for structured-output routes

carla: we should also add an eval metric: "structural-integrity" that checks for JSON parse success across canary prompts. Run across our existing toolcall dataset and measure regression vs baseline. If quantized model regresses > 0.5% absolute, fail canary.

elaine: agreed. I've already run a quick pass vs 2k toolcall prompts: parse success dropped from 99.4% -> 97.1% on quant canary when kvcache fast-stitch is enabled. Sharing the CSV that CI uploaded.

ci-bot: Deploy job r-2026-03-17-qt1 finished for raven-q8-v2 canary. test/struct-integrity: 97.1% (threshold 98.0%)

priya: okay actionable plan: 1) implement JSON-rescue hook on parse failure (short retry with explicit instruction + temp 0.0 + max_tokens 64), 2) change runtime to preserve safe suffix for structured-output endpoints, 3) add structural-integrity gate to canary.

zach: sample rescue prompt I use in other projects:
```
You are a JSON fixer. The user originally asked for a JSON object matching schema: {
  "items": [ { "id": string, "score": number } ],
  "meta": { "source": string }
}
The model output was: <MODEL_OUTPUT>
Return only the corrected JSON. Do not add any text.
```
Can call with decode settings: temperature=0.0, top_p=0.95, max_tokens=80, stop=["\n\n"].

elaine: nice. Also let's implement a lightweight detector that checks if the final token sequence ends in an incomplete UTF-8 codepoint or an unmatched bracket. If so, prefer a 2nd call to the model to continue rather than full retry. That has lower cost than a full regen.

matt: agree. For the runtime change, proposed config knobs:
```
service.struct_output_preserve_suffix_tokens = 256
service.struct_output_json_hard_check = true
kvcache.fast_stitch_drop_threshold = 0  # revert
```
We can gate by route-level metadata so only toolcall/funcall endpoints get this behavior.

carla: I'll add a canary check in the rollout pipeline: fail if struct-integrity < baseline - 0.5% or if mean time to repair (avg extra tokens / retries) > 0.2 tokens per call.

priya: also add logging for "parse_repair_invoked" with fields: model, quantized_flag, kvcache_prefix_len_bucket. That will help root-cause.

elaine: I'll implement the rescue hook + detector. Matt, can you PT the runtime revert or suffix-preserve change? Carla, can you add the canary gate? Priya/Zach, can you own the repair prompt and eval harness updates?

matt: yeah I'll open an eng-runtime PR with a revert/opt-in suffix preserve flag and a perf microbenchmark.

zach: I'll draft the rescue prompt variations and a small heuristic script to test for bracket matching. Quick regex I used: `re.search(r"[\]\}]$", s)` plus an unmatched bracket counter with a tiny stack.

elaine: thanks everyone. Quick follow-ups: please add short notes in the canary ticket with any perf impact numbers. For now I'm temporarily disabling fast-stitch on the quant canary to confirm.

carla: noted. will block rollout until we get integrity back to >=98%. :lock:

matt: PR 3742 opened: runtime: opt-in preserve-suffix-tokens for struct routes. bench shows 0.6% latency p99 uplift for preserve=256 on small tests. Sharing results in PR.

priya: I'll add the repair-hook to the inference client so it's available to hosted + private. We'll gate it behind a feature flag.

elaine: thanks — let's reconvene after the next canary run.

zach: one more micro suggestion — in the repair call, include last 16 tokens as context and set stop to the schema terminators. That usually forces a clean closing brace instead of free-form continuation.

elaine: good call. we'll try that.

matt: CI updated: new canary run scheduled.

ci-bot: Canary run started for raven-q8-v2 (flag: preserve-suffix=on).

elaine: perfect.
